thesis: The speakers argue that the diffusion of AI capability will take longer than anticipated because agents require durable, reliable backends rather than simpler systems, and that software must be built for agents when they outnumber employees by orders of magnitude. They contend that while agents can automate specific tasks, the fundamental nature of work shifts as humans must learn to think algorithmically and document complex flow charts to interface with these new tools, effectively moving the job up a rung of abstraction.
